passages.text: Then God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and settle there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jacob.
God said, “Get up.
Go to Bethel.
Live there.
Build an altar there.
Build it for the God who appeared to you.
He appeared to you when you ran away from Esau, your brother.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶֽל־ יַעֲקֹ֔ב ק֛וּם עֲלֵ֥ה בֵֽית־ אֵ֖ל וְשֶׁב־ שָׁ֑ם וַעֲשֵׂה־ שָׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לָאֵל֙ הַנִּרְאֶ֣ה אֵלֶ֔יךָ בְּבָרְחֲךָ֔ מִפְּנֵ֖י עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: So Jacob told his household and all who were with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you. Purify yourselves and change your garments.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the leader of his family.
Jacob spoke to his household.
Jacob also spoke to everyone with him.
Jacob said, “Remove the foreign gods that are among you.
Purify yourselves.
Change your garments.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־ בֵּית֔וֹ וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ הָסִ֜רוּ אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַנֵּכָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתֹכְכֶ֔ם וְהִֽטַּהֲר֔וּ וְהַחֲלִ֖יפוּ שִׂמְלֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then let us arise and go to Bethel. I will build an altar there to God, who answered me in my day of distress. He has been with me wherever I have gone.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham.
God spoke to Jacob.
Jacob spoke to his household and to all who were with him.
Jacob said, “Let us get up.
Let us go to Bethel.
I will build an altar there.
I will build it for God.
God answered me when I was in trouble.
God was with me on every journey I took.”
passages.original: וְנָק֥וּמָה וְנַעֲלֶ֖ה בֵּֽית־ אֵ֑ל וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ שָּׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֗חַ לָאֵ֞ל הָעֹנֶ֤ה אֹתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם צָֽרָתִ֔י וַיְהִי֙ עִמָּדִ֔י בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽכְתִּי׃

passages.text: So they gave Jacob all their foreign gods and all their earrings, and Jacob buried them under the oak near Shechem.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the leader of his household and all who were with him.
The people gave Jacob all the foreign gods they had in their hands.
They also gave him the earrings that were in their ears.
Jacob took these foreign gods and earrings.
Jacob buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
passages.original: וַיִּתְּנ֣וּ אֶֽל־ יַעֲקֹ֗ב אֵ֣ת כָּל־ אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַנֵּכָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָדָ֔ם וְאֶת־ הַנְּזָמִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאָזְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּטְמֹ֤ן אֹתָם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב תַּ֥חַת הָאֵלָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִם־ שְׁכֶֽם׃

passages.text: As they set out, a terror from God fell over the surrounding cities, so that they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.
passages.sermon: Jacob and his family began their journey.\r\nGod caused great fear to fall on the cities around them.\r\nThe people in those cities did not chase after Jacob’s sons.
passages.original: וַיִּסָּ֑עוּ וַיְהִ֣י׀ חִתַּ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֗ים עַל־ הֶֽעָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ סְבִיבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם וְלֹ֣א רָֽדְפ֔וּ אַחֲרֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: So Jacob and everyone with him arrived in Luz (that is, Bethel) in the land of Canaan.
passages.sermon:
Jacob traveled to Luz.
Luz is in the land of Canaan.
Luz is also called Bethel.
All the people with Jacob came with him to Luz.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב ל֗וּזָה אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן הִ֖וא בֵּֽית־ אֵ֑ל ה֖וּא וְכָל־ הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־ עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: There Jacob built an altar, and he called that place El-bethel, because it was there that God had revealed Himself to Jacob as he fled from his brother.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a man chosen by God.
Jacob arrived at Bethel in the land of Canaan.
Jacob built an altar there.
Jacob named that place El-bethel.
God had revealed Himself to Jacob at that place.
God appeared to Jacob when Jacob fled from his brother.
passages.original: וַיִּ֤בֶן שָׁם֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ וַיִּקְרָא֙ לַמָּק֔וֹם אֵ֖ל בֵּֽית־ אֵ֑ל כִּ֣י שָׁ֗ם נִגְל֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּבָרְח֖וֹ מִפְּנֵ֥י אָחִֽיו׃

passages.text: Now Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died and was buried under the oak below Bethel. So Jacob named it Allon-bachuth.
passages.sermon:
Deborah was Rebekah’s nurse.
Deborah died.
They buried Deborah under an oak tree.
The oak tree was below Bethel.
Jacob named the tree Allon-bachuth.
passages.original: וַתָּ֤מָת דְּבֹרָה֙ מֵינֶ֣קֶת רִבְקָ֔ה וַתִּקָּבֵ֛ר מִתַּ֥חַת לְבֵֽית־ אֵ֖ל תַּ֣חַת הָֽאַלּ֑וֹן וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ אַלּ֥וֹן בָּכֽוּת׃פ

passages.text: After Jacob had returned from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a man chosen by God.
Jacob returned from Paddan-aram.
God appeared to Jacob again.
God blessed Jacob.
passages.original: וַיֵּרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֶֽל־ יַעֲקֹב֙ ע֔וֹד בְּבֹא֖וֹ מִפַּדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֑ם וַיְבָ֖רֶךְ אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And God said to him, “Though your name is Jacob, you will no longer be called Jacob. Instead, your name will be Israel.” So God named him Israel.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jacob.
God said, “Your name is Jacob.
You will not be called Jacob anymore.
Your name will be Israel.”
God named him Israel.
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ ל֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים שִׁמְךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֑ב לֹֽא־ יִקָּרֵא֩ שִׁמְךָ֙ ע֜וֹד יַעֲקֹ֗ב כִּ֤י אִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־ שְׁמ֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And God told him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation—even a company of nations—shall come from you, and kings shall descend from you.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jacob.
God said, "I am God Almighty."
God told Jacob, "Be fruitful."
God told Jacob, "Multiply."
God said, "A nation will come from you."
God said, "A group of nations will come from you."
God said, "Kings will come from your descendants."
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֲנִ֨י אֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ פְּרֵ֣ה וּרְבֵ֔ה גּ֛וֹי וּקְהַ֥ל גּוֹיִ֖ם יִהְיֶ֣ה מִמֶּ֑ךָּ וּמְלָכִ֖ים מֵחֲלָצֶ֥יךָ יֵצֵֽאוּ׃

passages.text: The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you, and I will give this land to your descendants after you.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jacob.
God had already given land to Abraham.
God had already given land to Isaac.
God said, “I will give this land to you, Jacob.
I will also give this land to your descendants after you.”
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛תִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם וּלְיִצְחָ֖ק לְךָ֣ אֶתְּנֶ֑נָּה וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֥ אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ אֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Then God went up from the place where He had spoken with him.
passages.sermon: God had spoken with Jacob in a certain place.\r\nGod left Jacob in that place.\r\nGod went up from him.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַל מֵעָלָ֖יו אֱלֹהִ֑ים בַּמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So Jacob set up a pillar in the place where God had spoken with him—a stone marker—and he poured out a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham.
God spoke with Jacob at a certain place.
Jacob set up a pillar at that place.
The pillar was made of stone.
Jacob poured a drink offering on the stone pillar.
Jacob also poured oil on the stone pillar.
passages.original: וַיַּצֵּ֨ב יַעֲקֹ֜ב מַצֵּבָ֗ה בַּמָּק֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ מַצֶּ֣בֶת אָ֑בֶן וַיַּסֵּ֤ךְ עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ נֶ֔סֶךְ וַיִּצֹ֥ק עָלֶ֖יהָ שָֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: Jacob called the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham.
God spoke with Jacob at a certain place.
Jacob gave that place a name.
Jacob called the place Bethel.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת־ שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבֶּ֨ר אִתּ֥וֹ שָׁ֛ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בֵּֽית־ אֵֽל׃

passages.text: Later, they set out from Bethel, and while they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth, and her labor was difficult.
passages.sermon:
Jacob and his family left Bethel.
They traveled toward Ephrath.
They had not yet reached Ephrath.
Rachel began to give birth.
Her labor was difficult.
passages.original: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית אֵ֔ל וַֽיְהִי־ ע֥וֹד כִּבְרַת־ הָאָ֖רֶץ לָב֣וֹא אֶפְרָ֑תָה וַתֵּ֥לֶד רָחֵ֖ל וַתְּקַ֥שׁ בְּלִדְתָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: During her severe labor, the midwife said to her, “Do not be afraid, for you are having another son.”
passages.sermon:
Rachel was giving birth.
Her labor was very difficult.
A midwife was with her.
The midwife spoke to Rachel.
The midwife said, “Do not be afraid.”
The midwife said, “You are having another son.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י בְהַקְשֹׁתָ֖הּ בְּלִדְתָּ֑הּ וַתֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֤הּ הַמְיַלֶּ֙דֶת֙ אַל־ תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כִּֽי־ גַם־ זֶ֥ה לָ֖ךְ בֵּֽן׃

passages.text: And with her last breath—for she was dying—she named him Ben-oni. But his father called him Benjamin.
passages.sermon:
Rachel was dying.
She was giving birth.
She used her last breath to name her son Ben-oni.
The boy’s father was Jacob.
Jacob called his son Benjamin.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י בְּצֵ֤את נַפְשָׁהּ֙ כִּ֣י מֵ֔תָה וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בֶּן־ אוֹנִ֑י וְאָבִ֖יו קָֽרָא־ ל֥וֹ בִנְיָמִֽין׃

passages.text: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).
passages.sermon:
Rachel was Jacob’s wife.
Rachel died.
People buried Rachel on the way to Ephrath.
Ephrath is also called Bethlehem.
passages.original: וַתָּ֖מָת רָחֵ֑ל וַתִּקָּבֵר֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אֶפְרָ֔תָה הִ֖וא בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave; it marks Rachel’s tomb to this day.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was Rachel’s husband.
Rachel died.
Jacob set up a pillar on Rachel’s grave.
This pillar marks Rachel’s tomb.
People can still see this pillar today.
passages.original: וַיַּצֵּ֧ב יַעֲקֹ֛ב מַצֵּבָ֖ה עַל־ קְבֻרָתָ֑הּ הִ֛וא מַצֶּ֥בֶת קְבֻֽרַת־ רָחֵ֖ל עַד־ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Israel again set out and pitched his tent beyond the Tower of Eder.
passages.sermon:
Israel is Jacob.
Jacob traveled onward.
Jacob set up his tent.
He camped beyond the Tower of Eder.
passages.original: וַיִּסַּ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּ֣ט אָֽהֳלֹ֔ה מֵהָ֖לְאָה לְמִגְדַּל־ עֵֽדֶר׃

passages.text: While Israel was living in that region, Reuben went in and slept with his father’s concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard about it. Jacob had twelve sons: The sons of Leah were Reuben the firstborn of Jacob, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
passages.sermon:
Jacob is also called Israel.
Jacob lived in that land.
Reuben was Jacob’s oldest son.
Reuben went to Bilhah.
Bilhah was Jacob’s concubine.
Reuben slept with Bilhah.
Israel heard about this.
Jacob had twelve sons.
Leah was one of Jacob’s wives.
Leah’s sons were Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
Reuben was Jacob’s firstborn son.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁכֹּ֤ן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֔וא וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ רְאוּבֵ֔ן וַיִּשְׁכַּ֕ב֙ אֶת־ בִּלְהָ֖ה֙ פִּילֶ֣גֶשׁ אָבִ֑֔יו וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵֽ֑ל פ וַיִּֽהְי֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ יַעֲקֹ֖ב שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ בְּנֵ֣י לֵאָ֔ה בְּכ֥וֹר יַעֲקֹ֖ב רְאוּבֵ֑ן וְשִׁמְעוֹן֙ וְלֵוִ֣י וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְיִשָּׂשכָ֖ר וּזְבוּלֻֽן׃

passages.text: The sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.
passages.sermon: Rachel was Jacob’s wife.\r\nRachel had two sons.\r\nTheir names were Joseph and Benjamin.
passages.original: בְּנֵ֣י רָחֵ֔ל יוֹסֵ֖ף וּבִנְיָמִֽן׃

passages.text: The sons of Rachel’s maidservant Bilhah were Dan and Naphtali.
passages.sermon: Bilhah was Rachel’s maidservant.\r\nBilhah had two sons.\r\nTheir names were Dan and Naphtali.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֤י בִלְהָה֙ שִׁפְחַ֣ת רָחֵ֔ל דָּ֖ן וְנַפְתָּלִֽי׃

passages.text: And the sons of Leah’s maidservant Zilpah were Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan-aram.
passages.sermon:
Zilpah was Leah’s maidservant.
Zilpah had two sons.
Their names were Gad and Asher.
Jacob was their father.
Jacob’s sons were born to him in Paddan-aram.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה גָּ֣ד וְאָשֵׁ֑ר אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלַּד־ ל֖וֹ בְּפַדַּ֥ן אֲרָֽם׃

passages.text: Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac.
Jacob returned to his father Isaac.
Isaac was living at Mamre.
Mamre is near Kiriath-arba.
Kiriath-arba is also called Hebron.
Abraham and Isaac had lived at this place.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־ יִצְחָ֣ק אָבִ֔יו מַמְרֵ֖א קִרְיַ֣ת הָֽאַרְבַּ֑ע הִ֣וא חֶבְר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־ גָּֽר־ שָׁ֥ם אַבְרָהָ֖ם וְיִצְחָֽק׃

passages.text: And Isaac lived 180 years.
passages.sermon: Isaac was a patriarch.\r\nIsaac lived for 180 years.
passages.original: וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ יְמֵ֣י יִצְחָ֑ק מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֖ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the father of Esau and Jacob.
Isaac lived a long life.
Isaac became old.
Isaac was full of years.
Isaac breathed his last.
Isaac died.
Isaac was gathered to his people.
Esau and Jacob were Isaac’s sons.
Esau and Jacob buried Isaac.
passages.original: וַיִּגְוַ֨ע יִצְחָ֤ק וַיָּ֙מָת֙ וַיֵּאָ֣סֶף אֶל־ עַמָּ֔יו זָקֵ֖ן וּשְׂבַ֣ע יָמִ֑ים וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ עֵשָׂ֥ו וְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בָּנָֽיו׃פ
